title: Register governed remote browser backends (Kernel, Browserless, Browserbase) behind an egress-containment proof
summary: Expose the backend list and each backend's capability set through the session API, register the already-implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers behind config, and implement the containment proof that lets a remote driver run governed agent sessions (route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned egress proxy or require a provider-side egress allowlist attestation). Today Browserbase is scrape-only and Quarry rightly refuses backends that cannot prove isolated_egress.
whyItMatters: The local lease pool is a hard-coded 2 and one Chromium process, so burst capacity and reliability for the in-app browser and AI runs need a scale-out path that does not change Model Plane tools. Capability flags keep the governance story intact.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex multi-backend Browsers.list with per-backend capability sets (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-009 and codexbrowser-automation-and-safety-139, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (codex), unique; remote browser providers are common across scrapers
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: trait BrowserBackend { kind(); capabilities() -> Caps; open_session(); ... } registered at startup from config; the session API lists available backends ({type, family, profile, metadata}) and the planner or Model chooses by required capabilities (for example needs_user_login selects an extension backend, needs_isolated_egress selects a hosted one).

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/main.rs:316-327 (Browserbase registered for the scrape path with pool 4; no Kernel or Browserless registration found)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:85-89 (SSRF and DNS-pinning gates required for every remote provider before enabling for agents)
verevonToday.gap: BrowserDriver trait and capability flags exist and the local driver ships; Browserbase cannot run agent sessions (no isolated_egress); Kernel and Browserless are implemented but unregistered; there is no backend list on the session API and no user-browser or DOM-only backend.

approach: Ingestion Plane: register Kernel/Browserless behind config in main.rs, implement the egress-containment proof (provider traffic via Quarry's pinned proxy or an attested provider allowlist) and per-provider SSRF/redirect/subresource tests listed in the roadmap gates, then expose GET /v1/agent/backends with capabilities. Model Plane selects by required capabilities but never names a provider. Restrict managed providers to approved processor policies (ZDR, DPA).
dependencies: F-t2-007 (local pool) so remote and local capacity share one admission model
risks: Remote providers are data processors under ZDR and DPAs; the containment proof is hard to make real; provider outages need fallback to the local pool.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-03-09] apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md deliberate gate 2 (SSRF tests for every remote browser provider before enabling for agents) and SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md Phase 5 (managed providers only under approved processor policy)

verevon.exactGap: Capability flags and gates exist (BrowserDriverCapabilities, lib.rs:265-286; require_isolated_agent_egress and require_driver_capabilities, agent_routes.rs:1125-1217, with driver_requirements already accepted at 1305), but the agent path is hard-wired to one driver, state.agent_driver = ChromiumoxideDriver (main.rs:1283-1288), so there is nothing to register Kernel or Browserless into for agent runs; the scrape path has a single DriverKind::Browser slot that Browserbase takes before the local driver (main.rs:322-339). Kernel and Browserless are REST-only one-shot shims (kernel.rs:1-20, browserless.rs:1-12) constructed only in tests, and Browserbase never opens its connectUrl (browserbase.rs:5-12), so none of the three can serve ref-based actions, AX snapshots or live frames. The session API has a hard-coded capability list but no backend listing (browser.rs:2578, 2700), and per-run driver_capabilities are only echoed after a run exists (agent_routes.rs:543, 1658).
reuse: BrowserDriver trait, BrowserDriverCapabilities and the require_* gates in agent_routes
BrowserDriverAdapter::managed_provider with processor_id plus PrivacyPolicy.guard_third_party_processing (ZDR denies third-party processing even when the processor matches)
ChromiumoxideDriver code as the base for a CDP-attached remote driver (Browser::connect)
driver_requirements field already on the agent start body, per-run driver_capabilities in the response
ProfileStore for provider-agnostic persistent profiles; GAP.md 12.1 per-provider SSRF audit
verevon.constraints: Remote browsers are third-party processors: they need an approved processor policy and are refused under ZDR (privacy.rs tests), plus DPA review. Containment proof conflict: the pinned egress proxy endpoint type is loopback-only (lib.rs:331-360), which a remote browser cannot reach, so 'route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned proxy' contradicts that invariant, and GAP.md:450-462 records that Kernel and Browserbase only offer main-frame allowlists and that a real CDP connection is a prerequisite; the roadmap gate also requires redirect, iframe, XHR and subresource SSRF tests per provider before agent use (WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:85-89). Model proposes capability requirements and Quarry selects or rejects; the Model must never name a provider, and no driver_requirements usage was found in Model Plane Rust or Go sources.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-scope into three parts. (1) S to M, scrape path only: allow more than one managed browser driver by keying the registry beyond DriverKind::Browser (main.rs:322-339) and register Kernel or Browserless behind config with the existing managed_provider processor guard; this adds page-render burst capacity without touching agent governance. (2) XL for agent sessions: build a CDP-attached remote driver that reuses ChromiumoxideDriver over Browser::connect (the REST shims cannot do ref actions), replace the single state.agent_driver with a registry keyed by backend id, then implement and test the containment proof; keep Browserbase scrape-only until then. (3) S: expose GET /v1/agent/backends with capability sets and select by driver_requirements in start_run. Restrict managed providers to approved processor policies and non-ZDR runs.
verevon.effortNote: The item assumed the Kernel and Browserless drivers were ready to register. They are REST shims, so agent-capable remote backends need a new CDP-attached driver, a driver registry in AppState and a real containment proof.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial and already planned as a gate, but the central premise (register the implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers) is wrong for agent sessions and the proxy-based proof conflicts with the loopback-only invariant. Reword with the corrected split and a larger agent-session effort.
